scoring_justification: DFT-derived lattice constant and DOS peak cannot be recomputed by the lightweight verifier; the zT analytical model could be recomputed from the peak energy but that peak energy itself is a DFT output. Therefore result-level comparison against paper-reported values with tolerances is the feasible approach.

hidden_assets.purpose: Hidden gold values for lattice constant, DOS peak energy and height, and zT.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper-reported values: lattice constant 9.466 Å (text: 'Our calculation yields an equilibrium lattice constant a0 = 9.466 Å'), DOS peak energy 0.21 eV and height 200 states/(eV·unit cell) (from Fig. 3 caption and text), ideal zT 13.5 (text: 'we obtain the ideal zT=13.5 for Ce3Te4 at T=1200 K').
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the exact values reported in the paper; they are not invented and have clear traceable lineage.

outputs.description: Equilibrium lattice constant obtained from DFT structural relaxation.
Position (eV above Fermi level) and height of the delta‑shaped conduction‑band DOS peak.
Ideal thermoelectric figure of merit zT at 1200 K computed from the Mahan‑Sofo model.

output_contract.notes: All three outputs are compared to hidden reference values with tolerances appropriate for the chosen DFT implementation.

steps.description: Compare relaxed lattice constant to paper-reported 9.466 Å with tolerance ±0.05 Å.
Compare DOS peak energy and height to paper-reported values (0.21 eV, 200 states/(eV·unit cell)) with tolerances.
Compare computed ideal zT to paper-reported 13.5 with tolerance ±0.5.
